subject: Logic
title: Fallacies in Media
description: A micro-lesson that makes Fallacies in Media usable.

hook.text: A headline screams: "Study proves coffee cures cancer!" The study actually showed a weak correlation.

buildup.text: Media thrives on bold claims. Nuance gets cut; fallacies get amplified for clicks.

discovery.text: Cherry-picked stats, false dilemmas, and appeals to fear fill news cycles on every channel.

twist.text: Even credible outlets simplify complex findings. The error isn't always malice—it's deadlines and space.

climax.text: Read past headlines. Check the actual study. Ask what's missing, not just what's presented.

quiz.question: Why do media outlets often contain fallacies?
